summary: NOT EXISTS is true when a subquery produces no rows.
documentation: NOT EXISTS is true when a subquery produces no rows. A correlated subquery can identify outer records without a matching related record. Selected NULL values still count as existing rows.
inputs: A subquery, usually correlated with the outer row.
returns: A truth value indicating that no row matched.
caution: NOT IN can be affected by NULL values in its comparison set. An explicit correlated NOT EXISTS avoids that membership-list trap.
scenarios: Find products that have never been ordered.
List customers with no contact attempts recorded.
Identify scheduled jobs without a completion record.
title: Find products never ordered
problem: Tables products(id INTEGER, name TEXT) and order_lines(id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER). Return product id and name only when no order_lines row references that product id. NULL product_id values do not reference any product. Order by product id.
goal: Use NOT EXISTS or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Correlate the inner product_id to the outer product id, then negate EXISTS.
